budget.metric: relative error of the simulated tool life to the stated wear criterion (VB, VN), or of the simulated flank wear at a stated cutting time (VB(t) curve points)
budget.note: Set after a first run of the taylor_life harness had been seen (first-round report); justified only by the evidence below. Tool life amplifies every error of the wear-rate driver: with Taylor's law T ~ vc^(-1/n) a relative error e of the effective speed (or of the temperature-equivalent wear rate) changes the life by (1 + e)^(-1/n) - 1, i.e. -16/+22 % for e = +-10 % at the exponent n = 0.53 of the Aouici data and -32/+52 % at n = 0.25, before any scatter of the tests themselves. The lives are read off wear curves measured at intervals (case uncertainties 5 %), sources disagree with themselves by 10-17 % (Magalhaes 2026), and most series are single tests per speed. 50 % of the life is the narrowest bound that a wear model inside the temperature budget (15 % of the rise) can be expected to meet; it still rejects order-of-magnitude misses.
